Container.Name: PrintStash
Container.Overview: PrintStash is a self-hosted 3D print library and G-code vault. This image runs the web UI and API together. Create the first account in the browser from your local network, or set First-run setup to environment and fill in the administrator fields to create it at first start. The one appdata path stores everything PrintStash keeps: the database, uploaded files, thumbnails, staging files, backups, and caches. Add existing model folders as separate Library sources after setup; do not use an existing library as the appdata path. One image serves every server: to use an Intel or AMD GPU, enter /dev/dri in the optional GPU field; for NVIDIA, enable the NVIDIA runtime under Advanced View. Left blank, it runs on the CPU.

Container.Requires: Choose how the first administrator is created with First-run setup. With trusted_network (the default), leave the administrator fields blank and open the WebUI from your local network (tower.local or the server's LAN IP) to register in the browser; the first person to register becomes administrator, and registration through Tailscale, a VPN, a reverse proxy or a domain is refused. With environment, fill in the administrator username and password and PrintStash creates that account at first start. If the two do not fit together, setup stays closed and the WebUI explains what to change. When moving from the old two-container install, record the old API data owner first, then stop both old containers. Set PUID and PGID to that same owner (the old image usually used 10001:10001); otherwise existing Library sources can become unreadable. Follow the migration guide.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port to open PrintStash in your browser.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Dedicated persistent folder for everything PrintStash keeps: database, managed files, thumbnails, staging, backups, and caches. Keep it on one pool and add no second mapping for a subfolder of /data; imports then copy each file instead of using a hard-link. Do not map an existing model library here.

Config.Name: First-run setup
Config.Description: How the first administrator is created. trusted_network: in the browser, only from your local network (for example http://tower.local:3000 or the server's LAN IP); leave the administrator fields blank. environment: at first start from the administrator fields below, which are then required; choose this if you will first open PrintStash through Tailscale, a VPN, a reverse proxy or Unraid Connect.

Config.Name: Administrator username
Config.Description: Only with First-run setup set to environment: creates this administrator at first start; sign in with it and choose where files are stored. Leave blank with trusted_network, which creates the first administrator in the browser from your local network instead. Used once: it never changes an existing account.

Config.Name: Administrator password
Config.Description: Only with First-run setup set to environment: 8 to 256 characters. Used once: editing it later does not change the account; reset it under Settings, Users instead.

Config.Name: Administrator email
Config.Description: Optional, only with First-run setup set to environment: email for that administrator.

Config.Name: User ID
Config.Description: Numeric owner for appdata and mounted Library sources. Default is Unraid's nobody user. On upgrade, use the old API data owner's UID to keep existing Library sources readable.

Config.Name: Group ID
Config.Description: Numeric group for appdata and mounted Library sources. Default is Unraid's users group. On upgrade, use the old API data owner's GID to keep existing Library sources readable.

Config.Name: GPU: Intel or AMD (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Enter /dev/dri to let PrintStash use the server's Intel or AMD GPU; leave blank to run on the CPU. Nothing else is needed: Extra Parameters already allows the GPU device, and PrintStash joins the GPU's group by itself. For an NVIDIA GPU install the Nvidia Driver plugin, add --runtime=nvidia to Extra Parameters, and set the two NVIDIA fields under Advanced View.

Config.Name: GPU: NVIDIA visible devices
Config.Description: Optional, NVIDIA only (with --runtime=nvidia in Extra Parameters): the GPU UUID from the Nvidia Driver plugin, or all. Leave empty when not using an NVIDIA GPU.

Config.Name: GPU: NVIDIA driver capabilities
Config.Description: NVIDIA only. Keep all: graphics and compute are both needed for rendering.

Config.Name: GPU use
Config.Description: auto uses a GPU when the container can see one and falls back to the CPU otherwise; cpu never uses it. Settings, GPU shows what PrintStash found.

Config.Name: GPU render policy
Config.Description: qualified places work on the GPU only where a measured qualification receipt exists, so a new GPU stays on the CPU. preview lets you try the GPU for thumbnails and judge the result yourself.

Config.Name: GPU memory budget (MiB)
Config.Description: The most GPU memory PrintStash may plan to use, from 256 to 65536. It is an upper bound for admission, not a reservation; keep it below what other apps need from the card.

Config.Name: System memory budget: mesh work
Config.Description: Share of the server's RAM, from 0 to 1, that thumbnail and geometry work may reserve. Lower it on a small server that runs other containers; a dense model that does not fit is indexed without a preview instead of exhausting memory.

Config.Name: System memory budget: AI models
Config.Description: Share of the server's RAM, above 0 and below 1, that resident AI search models may hold. Applies when AI search is enabled.

Config.Name: Settings restart
Config.Description: Allows Settings to restart the supervised application container.
